originality.rationale: Jin--Lazarov--Zhou (arXiv:1404.3800), section 2.2, defines and applies second-order BDF CQ without the all-index tail-sign/monotonicity theorem. López-Fernández--Płociniczak (arXiv:2311.00081v3), section 2, eqs. (8)-(20) gives hypergeometric coefficients, 5/8 and 7/8 finite-index thresholds and explicitly reports only numerical verification of later negative signs and decreasing magnitudes. The thresholds and empirical observations are PRIOR KNOWLEDGE, not novel; the provable all-real-order, all-index induction and quantitative 3/4 adjacent ratio bounds are additional, not implied by finite numerical checks. A separate BDF2 scalar-decay positivity result concerns nonfractional trajectories and cannot imply fractional coefficient signs. No direct stronger proof was located; possible historical equivalence remains.
residual_risks: The all-index positivity and coefficient monotonicity may have been proved under other special-function or generating-function terminology not surfaced by the inspected searches.

The paper from 2023 already states the high-index sign pattern as a numerical observation; scientific originality lies in the first located rigorous uniform-in-order proof and ratio bounds, not the observed phenomenon itself.

value.rationale: The 2023 CQ energy/Grönwall analysis assumes negative convolution history weights and cites numerical checks for all higher BDF2 weights. A finite-step check cannot justify a uniform-in-history assumption. The present full-index analytic sign/monotonicity certificate and sharp failure orders provide a rigorous decision criterion for exactly that hypothesis; this is a meaningful structural result without claiming a new PDE convergence theorem.
